Well he summed up pretty much all I had to say about it. It seems like it just got popular from backlash for it's morality and edgier theme being marketed to "anarchists."

I don't think the game was actually being marketed to any consumer. The developers just cashed in on an increasingly puritanical games media who predictably gave it enormous amounts of free advertising. TotalBiscuit mentions Polygon writing eight articles about the game. That's the sort of advertising AAA budgets pay big bucks for. And every hyperbolic description of the game just makes people that much more interested.
This seems like a game I would have gone for when I was 14 and hopped up on testosterone.

I think this game should have either taken on a more satirical tongue-in-cheek approach, or went the other way and sent a message. The idea of a young man full of hatred could actually be topical in the current climate.

All they needed to do was give him a real reason to be annoyed, one that mirrors the real world. He mentions some wishy washy stuff about politics but there's nothing exact. Maybe he hates corruption or surveillance in particular, maybe he's unemployed, washed up, his family is disappointed with him, his friends have abandoned him or he never had any so he's turned to extreme violence, in the name of a god, maybe in the name of "Freedom".

I just think a better message could have been sent, something that maybe hit home. The character could have been easier to relate to, give an insight into how a person can turn into a monster.

An opportunity missed.
If this one is popular enough they could make a sequel.

I think the absurdity and complete lack of any grounding in reality is by design. The games media has been going increasingly puritanical so I know the guys developing this game knew they were going to get no coverage, in which case the game would flop, or they'd get this faux "outrage" coverage. The absurdity of the game paired against the hyperbolic coverage it received creates a great meta-story in my opinion since it most clearly illustrates how childish and immature the video games media has become.

If there actually was a compelling story here about some sort of sadistic revenge on society then the game might actually be disturbing. As is it just makes the games media look hilarious.

I'm not annoyed at this game because of the violence or subject matter per se, I'm annoyed because it seems so lazy. The devs are sure yelling a lot, but as it usually the case, the volume of the message is inversely proportional to its quality. Even the spree killer phenomenon could be interesting, but this isn't. What, exactly, is it trying to say? Mindless violence can be a fun escape or whatever, sure, but this doesn't even look like an especially fun or well-made version of that.

I think it's fair to compare this to certain movies in terms of not somehow cheapening the genre, so I agree with TB there. He's also exactly right when says that the hysteria from the games media is going to make this game more popular than it deserves to be, and this is usually the case with something like this. It's a pity the devs have decided to court controversy rather than make a good game, but caveat emptor. I don't find myself especially offended that this exists, because that would require a much greater impact on me than this is capable of evoking.
